input.question: Is there existing work that already trains language models on context-enriched triple subgraphs (i.e., not just isolated triples but also surrounding triples from the same passage) for multi-hop KGQA?
input.description: Determine if the core idea of enriching target triples with local context subgraphs from the same source passage has been explored.
input.rationale: If such work exists, the novelty claim is weakened; if not, the idea is novel.

text: Now second uncertainty: overlap with subgraph retrieval methods.

input.question: How much does the proposed method overlap with existing subgraph retrieval approaches like SG-RAG MOT or UniKGQA that already incorporate surrounding triple information?
input.description: Compare the proposed context-enriched triple training with methods that retrieve or use subgraphs for multi-hop QA.
input.rationale: Understanding overlap helps delineate the contribution (training on enriched triples vs retrieval-augmented inference).

text: Third uncertainty: validity of adaptive repair loop.

input.question: Does an adaptive repair loop that detects one-hop failures and generates corrective examples improve the reliability of base facts in language models trained on KG triples?
input.description: Check literature for adaptive repair, error-driven data augmentation, or iterative refinement in KGQA or relation extraction.
input.rationale: If such loops are ineffective or unexplored, the proposed mechanism may need revision.

text: Fourth uncertainty: feasibility of triple extraction at scale.

input.question: Can triples be reliably extracted from source passages at the scale needed for training, and what is the typical noise level of such extractions?
input.description: Investigate the performance of open-domain triple extraction tools (e.g., OpenIE, parser-based) on text passages used for KGQA.
input.rationale: If extraction is too noisy, the context subgraph may introduce harmful noise; if reliable, the assumption holds.
